paper_title: An analysis of vaccine-related sentiments from development to deployment   of COVID-19 vaccines
caption: : Polarity scores for Japan
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the distribution of polarity scores for vaccine-related sentiments in Japan, as analyzed in the paper “An analysis of vaccine-related sentiments from development to deployment of COVID-19 vaccines.” The x-axis, labeled “Polarity scores,” spans from -1.0 to 0.6 in linear increments of 0.2, representing the sentiment polarity ranging from strongly negative to moderately positive. The y-axis, labeled “Counts,” ranges from 0 to 40,000 in linear increments of 10,000, indicating the frequency of occurrences for each polarity score. A single blue line with circular markers connects data points, showing that counts are low and relatively flat between -1.0 and -0.6 (near 0 to 1,000), then rise gradually to about 5,000 at -0.6, dip slightly, and then increase sharply to a peak of approximately 42,000 at a polarity score of 0.0. After this peak, the counts drop steeply to around 8,000 at 0.1, rise again to about 26,000 at 0.2, fall to 9,000 at 0.3, dip to near 0 at 0.4, rise to 13,000 at 0.5, and fall again to near 0 at 0.6. The plot highlights a strong concentration of sentiment around neutral polarity (0.0), with a secondary peak at 0.2, and relatively sparse positive sentiment beyond 0.3.
